exposure: Social support (measured using the Social Provisions Scale (SPS))
outcome: Anxiety levels (measured using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS))
finding: Higher antenatal anxiety and depression scores were associated with lower social support, rural background, history of harassment, abortion, cesarean delivery, unplanned pregnancies, and having more daughters.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was significantly associated with higher levels of anxiety and depression during pregnancy.
